releases.title: Launch items and a menu bar monitor panel
releases.summary: Identifies login and background launch sources with controlled disable and restore, and redesigns the status bar live monitoring panel.
highlights: New launch items page identifying user and shared LaunchAgents, LaunchDaemons, and the current user's visible login and background tasks, showing source, launch conditions and state.

Supports disabling qualifying user launch configurations after confirmation, keeping integrity-checked restorable backups; running tasks are not killed and new configurations at the restore location are never overwritten.
System-managed login items and background tasks link to the native System Settings; items that cannot be managed directly state why.
The status bar menu upgrades to a dark graphite frosted monitoring panel with rounded segments, hairline strokes and teal data bars, offering Overview and Processes views.
The panel shows CPU, memory, disk, network, real trend charts and top consumers, with pause, resume, open main window and settings.
The status bar label gains a monospace CPU readout; the panel reuses existing sampling with no separate timers or duplicate collection.
notes: Disable and restore only run after explicit confirmation; existing launch items are never changed automatically.
Launch-at-login, background and on-demand services are different things; an enabled state does not mean the process is currently running.
No privilege escalation and no resets of the background tasks database; system or admin-managed items must be handled via System Settings or their owning app.
No online update source is configured yet; this release still uses the local build, install and distribution flow.

releases.title: Browser diagnostics, version history and local install
releases.summary: Adds instance diagnostics and controlled exit for AI automation browsers, plus version, update history and local installation.
highlights: New browser diagnostics: reads real launch arguments and identifies automation instances by process tree and isolated profile directory, showing launch source, headless flag, executable path and an RSS estimate.

Supports confirmed per-instance exit with a read-back of survivors; after the main process exits, surviving renderers whose identity still matches the original snapshot can be explicitly force-quit. Everyday browsers and Electron apps are protected as whole groups.
Settings gains version and update info: current version, build number, build time, source summary, running path and installed state.
Full local update history preserving the first release notes; the in-app history and CHANGELOG.md are generated from the same data and validated.
Info.plist is the version source of truth; the build validates history records and stamps actual build time, source SHA-256 and Git source state.
Standard installation to /Applications/cduyzhProcessTool.app: the staged bundle is verified first, then swapped atomically, with a compressed backup of the old version and restore on failure.
Checks for running instances of this product before installing and refuses to overwrite by default; --quit-running explicitly stops processes verified by executable path.
Local release packaging script producing versioned ZIPs, SHA-256 checksums and release metadata.
notes: Being headless, long-running, parented to PID 1, or located in a temp directory does not alone prove a leftover process. Nothing is killed automatically and no browser data is deleted.
No online update source is configured yet; this release never contacts an update server and never claims to be remotely up to date.
Local builds are ad-hoc signed without Developer ID signing or Apple notarization.
0.1.0 and 0.2.0 are local development release records, not public releases.

releases.title: First local development release
releases.summary: Presents processes, resources and ports in a native macOS interface, prioritizing the UI and icon design with real local sampling.
highlights: A native three-column interface in mist white with teal accents: sidebar navigation, resource cards, process list and detail panel.
Original chip-pulse app icon, multi-size ICNS, and a unified SF Symbols icon language.
CPU, memory, startup disk capacity, physical network throughput and real sampled trends, with pause and manual refresh.
Process search, sorting, app/background filters, persistent watch by executable path, path copy and Finder reveal.
On-demand TCP LISTEN and UDP bound endpoints with search, sorting, copy and jump to the owning process.
Confirmed quit and force quit that re-verify user, PID and microsecond-precision start time before acting, protecting system, self and other users' processes.
CSV export of the current list, menu bar resource status, sampling interval and light/dark appearance settings.
Dependency-free SwiftPM build and local app packaging with a fixed Bundle ID.
notes: Requires macOS 14 or later; process and port details are limited by local system permissions.
Process CPU treats one logical core as 100%; total CPU is normalized across all cores; process memory is RSS.
The first CPU and network sample needs a second sample for deltas; the disk card shows capacity, not disk I/O.
